newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big SPX exercise seen on Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big SPX exercise seen on Friday.

text.p: Thin trading in S&P 500 index options on Thursday suggested that a big exercise would take place at the opening on Friday, traders said.
Traders said they were leaning toward a buy-side bias for the early exercise on Friday.
At the same time, more exercises on S&P 100 index options were expected as OEX volume remained heavy.
"There was a small exercise last night," one OEX trader said. "It will probably be tonight but we won't know until the end of the day."
By 1430 CDT (1930 GMT), about 27,400 contracts in the OEX September 660 traded, making it the most active index option. Its open interest through Wednesday was 17,660.
The September 660 call had the highest open interest of any OEX option.
"The OEX is winding down nicely," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co., "It looks like a high percentage of the open interest is coming down."
The OEX September 655 call, with open interest of 17,485, traded about 15,200 contracts. The 665 call, with open interest of 15,900, traded about 14,160.
On the put side, the September 655 traded nearly 21,500 contracts. Its open interest was 17,567.
With the spot OEX up 1.30 at 660.74, the September 655 put was down 1-1/16, trading at 11/16.
The September 660 put, down 1-7/8 at 1-3/4, traded mroe than 19,000 contracts. Its open interest was 11,900.
The SPX option with the highest open interest was the September 650 call, which traded about 850 contracts. Its open interest was 32,560.
The most active September SPX option was the 680 call, which traded more than 7,300 contracts. Its open interest was 13,709.

"Looking at SPX open interest and volume, there's not much unwinding going on," Schwartz said. "I've got a feeling that the imbalance, because of the significant number of deep in-the-money calls could generate a disproportionate number of buy orders in the morning."
He added that checking open interest after Thursday's close would help determine whether the imbalance would indeed be on the buy side Friday morning.
Other busy September SPX options included the 675 put, the 680 put, the 685 call and the 690 call.
In October, the October 675 call traded about 8,500 contracts, making it the most active. The option was up 1/4 at 16-1/2 and its open interest was roughly 3,900.
The spot SPX was up 1.45 points at 682.92.
--Gregory Crawford, derivatives desk, (312) 408-8750
